GoThru SSO Integration Guide

This guide explains how another GoThru application can integrate with GoThru SSO
using the same pattern used by Panorra PWA. The examples are language-neutral so
they can be applied to JavaScript, PHP, Go, Python, Java, mobile apps, or any
backend stack.

Flow Overview

The recommended integration is:

User opens your app
  -> frontend redirects to GoThru Keycloak login
  -> user signs in with GoThru
  -> frontend receives a Keycloak access token
  -> frontend sends that token to your backend
  -> backend verifies the token with Keycloak
  -> backend creates or finds the local app user
  -> backend returns your app session/JWT

The frontend proves that the browser login completed. The backend must verify
the token again before creating a local application session.

Keycloak Client Setup

Create one Keycloak client for each GoThru application.

For browser-based apps:

  • Client type: public
  • Client authentication: off
  • Standard flow: enabled
  • PKCE: S256
  • Valid redirect URI: https://your-app.example.com/callback
  • Web origin: https://your-app.example.com
  • Scopes: openid profile email

Do not put a Keycloak client secret in a frontend app. Browser and mobile apps
cannot keep a client secret private.

For server-side apps that exchange the authorization code on the backend:

  • Client type: confidential
  • Client authentication: on
  • Store KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET only on the backend
  • The frontend or browser should never receive the client secret

Frontend Contract

Every app needs these values:

GOTHRU_SSO_URL=https://id.gothru.org
GOTHRU_SSO_REALM=gothru
GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID=your-app-client-id
GOTHRU_SSO_REDIRECT_URI=https://your-app.example.com/callback

For development, use the dev Keycloak URL and the app's local callback URL:

GOTHRU_SSO_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
GOTHRU_SSO_REALM=gothru
GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID=your-app-client-id
GOTHRU_SSO_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:4200/callback

Frontend pseudocode:

create Keycloak/OIDC client with:
  url = GOTHRU_SSO_URL
  realm = GOTHRU_SSO_REALM
  clientId = GOTHRU_SSO_CLIENT_ID
  pkce = S256

redirect user to login

on callback:
  initialize OIDC client
  read access_token
  POST access_token to backend /auth/gothru
  receive local app session token
  store local app session using the app's normal session strategy

For Panorra PWA, this is implemented with keycloak-js and a /callback
route. Other frameworks can use their normal OIDC client library as long as they
use authorization code flow with PKCE.

Backend Contract

Every backend needs these values:

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://auth.gothru.co
KEYCLOAK_URL=https://auth.gothru.co
KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=your-api-audience

For the current dev Keycloak server:

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=your-api-audience

KEYCLOAK_URL can be kept as a fallback alias for services that already read
that name. New services should prefer KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL.

Backend Login Endpoint

Expose a backend endpoint similar to Panorra's:

POST /auth/gothru
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "access_token": "<keycloak_access_token>"
}

Successful response should return the application's own session:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "code": "success",
    "token": "<local_app_session_token>",
    "user": {
      "id": "local-user-id",
      "email": "user@example.com",
      "username": "username"
    }
  }
}

The local app token is not the Keycloak token. It is the token your own app uses
for API requests after login.

Backend Verification Options

Use one of these verification approaches.

Option A: Userinfo Verification

This is the simplest implementation and matches the current Panorra backend.

Backend pseudocode:

read access_token from request body
reject if missing

GET {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Accept: application/json

if Keycloak returns 401 or 403:
  return 401 Unauthorized

if Keycloak returns non-2xx:
  return 502 Cannot verify GoThru token

read userinfo:
  sub
  email
  email_verified
  preferred_username
  name
  given_name
  family_name

find local user by keycloak sub
if not found:
  create or explicitly link local user

create local app session/JWT
return local app session/JWT

This works in any backend language because it is only an HTTP request to
Keycloak.

Option B: JWT/JWKS Verification

This is stronger and better for high-traffic APIs because the backend validates
the Keycloak JWT locally.

Backend requirements:

  • Fetch JWKS from:
    {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}/protocol/openid-connect/certs
  • Cache signing keys
  • Validate RS256 only
  • Validate issuer:
    {KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL}/realms/{KEYCLOAK_REALM}
  • Validate expiry
  • Validate audience when your Keycloak client is configured to include it
  • Use sub as the stable external user ID

Do not trust decoded JWT claims before signature validation succeeds.

User Mapping

Every app should store a link between the local user and Keycloak:

local_user_id
keycloak_sub
keycloak_email
keycloak_username
realm_name
linked_at

Use keycloak_sub as the stable identity. Email and username can change, so
they should not be the permanent link.

Recommended behavior:

  • Existing linked user: log in normally
  • New GoThru user: create local user or start onboarding
  • Existing local user with same verified email: link only if the product has
    approved this behavior
  • Unverified email: do not silently link accounts by email

Error Handling

Return safe, generic errors to the frontend:

Missing token -> 400
Invalid or expired token -> 401
Token verified, but local user is blocked -> 403
Backend cannot reach Keycloak -> 502
Unexpected app failure -> 500

Useful troubleshooting:

  • unauthorized_client: Keycloak client is probably confidential, has wrong
    redirect URI, or has invalid client settings for a public SPA.
  • Invalid client or Invalid client credentials: frontend is using a public
    flow against a client that requires a secret.
  • Cannot verify GoThru token: backend cannot verify the token with Keycloak.
    Check KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL, KEYCLOAK_REALM, network access, and token expiry.
  • aud is account: the token is valid for Keycloak account APIs. Configure an
    audience mapper if your backend validates a custom API audience.

Security Checklist

  • Use HTTPS in production.
  • Use authorization code flow with PKCE for browser/mobile apps.
  • Never store a Keycloak client secret in frontend code.
  • Treat access tokens like passwords. Do not paste them into tickets, chats, or
    logs.
  • Verify the token on the backend before creating an app session.
  • Use sub as the permanent external identity.
  • Validate token expiry.
  • Prefer JWKS validation for production APIs when possible.
  • Log diagnostic errors without logging full tokens or authorization headers.
  • Keep app session lifetime independent from the Keycloak access token lifetime.

Panorra Reference

Panorra PWA uses this pattern:

Angular callback route
  -> keycloak-js obtains Keycloak access token
  -> POST /auth/keycloak to app2-dev.panorra.com or app2.panorra.com
  -> Go backend calls Keycloak userinfo
  -> backend creates Panorra JWT
  -> frontend stores Panorra session

Other GoThru apps can keep the same contract while replacing Angular, Go, or
Fiber with their own framework.

issues.display_title: Issue #1876: feat(blog): integrate public blog and category endpoints in BlogAdminService and BlogService
issues.main_description_html:
Background & Problem

Currently, BlogService and BlogAdminService use the support endpoint GET /v1/support/blog/articles (Backend Issue GoThruMedia/villume-backend-go#199) indiscriminately for both admin management and public article queries. Because /v1/support/blog/* strictly requires JWT authentication and a support role, unauthenticated visitors and non-support accounts encounter 401 Unauthorized errors when viewing published articles on public views (such as the landing page / and public journal /blog).

The backend has implemented dedicated public endpoints that are excluded from JWT authentication and strictly return published records:

  • GET /v1/blog/articles (Backend Issue GoThruMedia/villume-backend-go#191): Public article listing with pagination and server-side filtering.
  • GET /v1/blog/categories (Backend Issue GoThruMedia/villume-backend-go#192): Public category list with published articles_count.
  • GET /v1/blog/tags (Backend Issue GoThruMedia/villume-backend-go#193): Public deduplicated tags list.

Scope of Work

  1. BlogAdminService (src/app/pages/blog-admin/blog-admin.service.ts):

    • Define interface BlogPublicListParams: 
      export interface BlogPublicListParams {
  page?: number;
  limit?: number;
  search?: string;
  category?: string; // slug or UUID
  tag?: string;
  featured?: string | boolean; // 'true' or '1'
}
    • Implement getPublicArticles(params?: BlogPublicListParams): Observable<BlogListResponse> calling GET /v1/blog/articles.
    • Implement getPublicCategories(): Observable<BlogCategory[]> calling GET /v1/blog/categories.
    • Maintain existing getArticles() and getCategories() for support management calls to /v1/support/blog/*.
    • Provide fallback to local in-memory published articles/categories if request fails or offline.

  2. BlogService (src/app/pages/blog/blog.service.ts):

    • Update getPublicPosts(options?: BlogFilterOptions) to call blogAdminService.getPublicArticles(...).
    • Update getFeaturedPosts(limit?: number) to call blogAdminService.getPublicArticles({ featured: 'true', limit }).
    • Update getRelatedPosts(currentPost, limit?: number) to use blogAdminService.getPublicArticles({ category: currentPost.category }) instead of querying the support endpoint.
    • Update loadCategoriesFromBackend():
      • If user is support (user_type === 'support' || supportSession.hasSupportSession()), fetch from getCategories().
      • Otherwise, fetch from getPublicCategories().

Acceptance Criteria

  • getPublicArticles invokes GET /v1/blog/articles without requiring an Authorization header.
  • Query parameters page, limit, search, category, tag, and featured are serialized correctly.
  • getPublicCategories invokes GET /v1/blog/categories and maps articles_count.
  • Public-facing methods (getPublicPosts, getFeaturedPosts, getRelatedPosts) in BlogService query the public endpoints rather than /v1/support/blog/*.
  • Unit tests in blog-admin.service.spec.ts pass and cover both successful responses and mock fallbacks.

issues.display_title: Issue #1877: feat(blog): condition blog view and navigation for support vs public and non-support accounts
issues.main_description_html:
Background & Problem

In BlogListComponent, the view mode isInsideDashboard is currently evaluated as !!this.mainService.userInfo. As a result, any logged-in user (such as regular artists, collectors, or gallery clients) is presented with the Admin Dashboard view (dash-blog-admin). This causes two issues:

  1. The component attempts to fetch /v1/support/blog/articles via getAdminPosts(), which fails with 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden for non-support accounts.
  2. The UI exposes admin-only controls ("Create Blog", publish/unpublish toggles, edit actions). The "Create Blog" link points to /blog/new, which is protected by authSupportGuard and redirects to /404.

Additionally, the desktop sidemenu currently renders a "Create blog" submenu item for all logged-in users under /blog.

Scope of Work

  1. BlogListComponent (src/app/pages/blog/blog-list/blog-list.component.ts):

    • Inject SupportSessionService.
    • Define isSupportUser: 
      public get isSupportUser(): boolean {
  return this.supportSession.shouldShowSupportMenu(this.mainService.userInfo);
}
    • Condition isInsideDashboard: 
      public get isInsideDashboard(): boolean {
  return this.isSupportUser;
}
    • Update loadData() and applyFilters():
      • When isSupportUser: call blogService.getAdminPosts(filterOptions).
      • When not support (unauthenticated or regular logged-in user): call blogService.getPublicPosts(filterOptions).
    • In blog-list.component.html, ensure the "Create New" hero button in the public view is displayed only if isLoggedIn && isSupportUser.

  2. SidemenuComponent (src/app/layouts/sidemenu/sidemenu.component.ts & .html):

    • Inject SupportSessionService or verify support role on userInfo.
    • Wrap the "Create blog" submenu link with @if (isSupportUser) so non-support logged-in accounts only see the main "Blog" link.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Unauthenticated visitors navigating to /blog see the Full Public Marketing View (The Villume Journal) and consume GET /v1/blog/articles.
  • Logged-in non-support users (e.g. user_type: 'user') navigating to /blog see the Full Public Marketing View without admin controls.
  • Support accounts (user_type: 'support' or active support session) navigating to /blog see the Admin Dashboard view (dash-blog-admin) and consume /v1/support/blog/articles.
  • Non-support logged-in accounts do not see the "Create blog" submenu in the sidemenu.
  • Unit tests in blog-list.component.spec.ts verify correct routing of data fetching and layout based on account type.
  • Project compiles cleanly via pnpm ng build --configuration=development.

  3. Article Structured Data (Rich Snippets):
    • Add standard article structured data (Schema.org) so search engines can recognize and showcase Villume blog posts as rich results.
  4. Sitemap & Robots Update:
    • Register the blog and key public pages in the sitemap while retaining legacy domain entries.

Acceptance Criteria
